result.spec:
BOOKS-06 — THE REAL FIX: BIGINT MONEY COLUMNS. Architect build spec (read-only pass, 2026-10-12, repo /home/user/servd at HEAD e813299 + the storefront workflow's uncommitted files).

Everything below was checked in scratch, outside the repo. The checks: Prisma 5.22.0 probes against Postgres 16.13; a copy of backend/ type-checked with the columns widened; a migration rehearsal with all 192 RLS policies in place; and the FULL backend suite run against a prototype of the boundary. The repo, its generated client and every database other than my own scratch ones were not touched. My scratch DBs are dropped.

Prototype result: with only the widened schema and the boundary below, and no other code change, the full suite gave 125 of 127 files and 1936 of 1938 tests green. The two failures are expected; see §6. tsc reports 122 errors in 26 files, listed in §3a. These errors block `npm run build`.

==================================================================
0. DECISIONS (summary)
==================================================================
- Widen 40 INT4 columns on 22 tables to BIGINT in ONE migration: backend/prisma/migrations/20261012140000_money_bigint/migration.sql.
  - bank_statement_imports.openingBalanceCents and closingBalanceCents are already BIGINT (migration 20261010150000). They join the same mechanism, giving 42 BIGINT money fields on 23 models.
- PRIMARY BOUNDARY: one Prisma QUERY extension, `moneyAsNumbers`, in the new file backend/src/lib/money.ts.
  - It is installed on the single raw client in lib/prisma.ts, UNDER the RLS extension.
  - It turns every bigint in every model-operation result into a JS number. That covers rows, include/select at any depth, fluent relations, _sum/_min/_max, groupBy, create/update/upsert/delete/createManyAndReturn.
  - It applies on `prisma`, on `serviceClient`, and on every $transaction client, in both the callback and the array form.
  - Clients keep receiving plain JSON numbers. No response shape changes.
- SAFETY NET: an idempotent BigInt.prototype.toJSON that returns toCents(this). It gives a JSON number, and throws beyond MAX_SAFE_INTEGER instead of rounding. It is installed from lib/prisma.ts.
  - It is a net only. The extension is the mechanism of record.
  - Do NOT add `declare global { interface BigInt { toJSON } }`. In the prototype it made bigint assignable to Prisma.InputJsonValue and hid a real site (procurement/service.ts:175) from tsc.
- TYPES: Prisma keeps typing the widened fields as `bigint`. `prisma` and `serviceClient` stay typed PrismaClient. Fix the 122 tsc errors with toCents()/sumCents(), or by widening helper parameters to DbMoney.
  - toCents() and sumCents() accept bigint | number. That makes them correct on a raw client too.
  - No bigint literals, no BigInt(), no bigint arithmetic, and no `as never`/`as unknown` casts on DB writes in src/.
- CEILINGS:
  - MAX_MONEY_CENTS = 90_000_000_000_000 paisa (PKR 900,000,000,000.00) per amount on BIGINT columns. That is about MAX_SAFE_INTEGER/100, so any sum of up to 100 maximal amounts is still exact in JS.
  - Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9,007,199,254,740,991 paisa (≈ PKR 90.07 trillion) is the hard ceiling. toCents() throws 500 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE beyond it rather than rounding. Postgres BIGINT (9.22e18) is never the binding limit.
  - INT4_MAX_CENTS = 2,147,483,647 (PKR 21,474,836.47) stays for the INT4 columns: till, orders, payments, per-unit stock cost.

==================================================================
1. COLUMN LIST
==================================================================
IN — Int to BigInt, keeping defaults and nullability. Edit schema.prisma by hand and do NOT run `prisma format`.

Ledger
- JournalLine.amountCents: opening balances, capital injections, loans, group payroll accruals, allocations and capex exceed PKR 21.47m in one line.

- SupplierPayment: amountCents, appliedCents.

Customer

  - After that, recomputeCustomerRollups' update fails and bumpCustomerRollups swallows the error.
  - That customer's lastOrderAt, firstOrderAt and no-show rollups then freeze silently, which breaks CRM segments and referrals.
  - Writes come from _sum of Order.totalCents (INT4), so no other change is needed.

OUT — stay INT4:
- Per ticket and till. A single restaurant bill never nears PKR 21m, and the guards are KEPT:
  - Order.* and OrderItem/OrderItemModifier prices.
  - Payment.*, Shift floats, CashMovement, TerminalCharge.*, PreBill.*.

  - InventoryItem.unitCostCents and listPriceCents.
  - ItemPriceHistory.oldCostCents and newCostCents.
  - GoodsReceiptLine.poUnitCostCents.
  - WasteLog, StaffMeal, Recipe.actualSellingPriceCents, and menu and modifier prices.
- Per person (HR): User.hourlyRateCents, PayrollRunLine.*, HrEmployee.*, HrPayslip.*, HrRecord.amountCents, Position.*, KitchenStaff, KitchenPayrollRun, WageSettings.

- No write path in the API (checked by grep):

  - CapitalLedgerEntry.amountCents: read-only history.

  - PayrollRun.totalGrossCents: legacy, no writer.
  - FinancialEntry.*: aggregator era.
- Config, thresholds and per-check planning: RefundPolicy, ReceiptConfig, OperationsConfig, ReservationPolicy, DeliveryZone, TierConfig, ProFormaChannel.checkAvgCents, ProFormaFixedCost.monthlyCents, ProjectionBrandInput.checkAverageCents.
- TenantContribution.monthlyCents: head-office contribution of about PKR 0.5m a month.

==================================================================
2. THE BOUNDARY — WHAT WAS VERIFIED, AND WHY THE QUERY EXTENSION
==================================================================
Option A — a result extension shadowing the real field (`result: { journalLine: { amountCents: { needs: { amountCents: true }, compute: r => Number(r.amountCents) } } }`). The shadowing is allowed.
- (+) Numbers for find*, create, update (including increment), upsert, delete and createManyAndReturn; for select and include; for nested include in both directions; and inside $transaction in both forms.
  - The last point holds ONLY if the extension sits on the client whose $transaction the RLS override delegates to, which is basePrisma.
- (−) The fluent API (`findUnique(...).lines()`) still returns bigint.
- (−) aggregate _sum/_min/_max and groupBy _sum still return bigint (_avg is a number).
- (−) $queryRaw is untouched.
- (−) Rows become Proxies, and structuredClone throws DataCloneError.
- (−) The number TYPES exist only if the extended client type is exported, and lib/prisma.ts casts to PrismaClient. I measured exporting it:
  - 277 tsc errors in 50 files.
  - The tx client is not assignable to Prisma.TransactionClient/PrismaClient in orders, auth, hr, connectors and other modules.
  - TS2349 "not callable" on Tx unions, and TS2321 "excessive stack depth" in auth.
  - tsc takes 45 s against 24 s.

Option B — a query extension that walks each result. CHOSEN.
- `query: { $allModels: { $allOperations } }` with bigintsToNumbers(await query(args)).
- (+) Numbers everywhere, verified for:
  - Rows, and include/select at any depth, including a non-BIGINT model selecting a BIGINT relation.
  - Fluent relations, aggregate _sum/_max, groupBy _sum.
  - Create, update with increment and decrement, upsert, delete, createManyAndReturn.
  - Nullable columns (null stays null).
  - prisma.$transaction(fn) and prisma.$transaction([...]); serviceClient and serviceClient.$transaction.
  - RLS_ENFORCE=0 and =1, with and without an RLS context.
- (+) Rows stay plain objects.
- (−) $queryRaw and $executeRaw are not model operations:
  - int8 comes back as bigint.
  - SUM(int8) comes back as Prisma.Decimal, which JSON.stringify writes as a STRING.
  - SUM(int4) comes back as bigint; `::float8` comes back as a number.
  - No raw SQL in src/ reads a widened column today (checked by grep: they are FOR UPDATE locks and existence checks only). crm and analytics raw SQL read orders and counts and already use Number().
- Cost: one in-place walk of each result that belongs to a BIGINT model or uses include/select. I measured 0–30 % on 200k–500k-row reads on a noisy box; it is negligible at API result sizes.
- Writes need no change: Prisma accepts JS numbers for BIGINT inputs, filters and increment/decrement. But:
  - It silently rounds numbers above 2^53 (9007199254740993 was stored as …992).
  - It throws PrismaClientValidationError (500) for non-integers and for values above 2^63.
  - So every BIGINT write path is capped (§4).

Option C — convert at each read site. Rejected.
- The runtime is bigint everywhere. tsc flags the same 122 sites but misses:
  - JSON responses.
  - bigint/bigint division, which truncates (paid/total gives 0).
  - Map<number> keys (2n !== 2; reconciliation/service.ts byAmount).
  - Json metadata.
- The names amountCents, totalCents and taxCents are shared with INT4 models (918 references to amountCents), so the read sites cannot be found by grep.
- The existing BankStatementImport code (Number() on read, BigInt() on write) IS this approach. It is replaced, so there is ONE approach.

Option D — a global toJSON alone. Rejected as the primary approach.
- It fixes JSON only. `reduce((s,l)=>s+l.amountCents,0)` throws "Cannot mix BigInt and other types"; I observed this in journal.test.ts with a raw client.

2a. backend/src/lib/money.ts (NEW). The exact API is load-bearing; this code compiled and was exercised in the scratch copy:
```ts
import { Prisma } from '@prisma/client'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { AppError } from './errors.js'          // errors.ts imports nothing, so there is no cycle
export const INT4_MAX_CENTS = 2_147_483_647     // INT4 columns: PKR 21,474,836.47
export const MAX_MONEY_CENTS = 90_000_000_000_000 // one BIGINT amount: PKR 900,000,000,000.00
export type DbMoney = number | bigint           // as Prisma TYPES it; at runtime always a number
export function toCents(v: DbMoney): number
export function toCents(v: DbMoney | null): number | null
export function toCents(v: DbMoney | null | undefined): number | null | undefined
export function toCents(v: DbMoney | null | undefined): number | null | undefined {
  if (v === null || v === undefined) return v
  const n = typeof v === 'bigint' ? Number(v) : v
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(n)) throw new AppError('AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE', `A money value (${String(v)} paisa) is outside the exact range`, 500)
  return n
}
/** _sum/_min/_max of a BIGINT column; no rows (null) → 0. NEVER for _avg (float). */
export function sumCents(v: DbMoney | null | undefined): number { return v == null ? 0 : toCents(v) }
const pkr = (c: number) => `PKR ${(c / 100).toLocaleString('en-PK', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`
export function amountTooLarge(what: string, cents?: number, max: number = MAX_MONEY_CENTS): AppError {
  const got = cents !== undefined && Number.isFinite(cents) ? ` comes to ${pkr(cents)}, which is` : ' is'
  return new AppError('AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE', `${what}${got} more than the ${pkr(max)} one amount can be — check the figure`, 422)
}
export function assertMoneyFits(cents: number, what: string): void { if (!Number.isFinite(cents) || Math.abs(cents) > MAX_MONEY_CENTS) throw amountTooLarge(what, cents) }
export function assertInt4Fits(cents: number, what: string): void { if (!Number.isFinite(cents) || Math.abs(cents) > INT4_MAX_CENTS) throw amountTooLarge(what, cents, INT4_MAX_CENTS) }
type Sign = 'positive' | 'nonnegative' | 'any'
export function zMoneyCents(what: string, opts: { sign?: Sign; max?: number } = {}) {
  const max = opts.max ?? MAX_MONEY_CENTS
  const int = z.number().int()
  const base = opts.sign === 'positive' ? int.positive() : opts.sign === 'any' ? int : int.nonnegative()
  return base.transform((v) => { if (Math.abs(v) > max) throw amountTooLarge(what, v, max); return v })
}
export const zInt4Cents = (what: string, opts: { sign?: Sign } = {}) => zMoneyCents(what, { ...opts, max: INT4_MAX_CENTS })
export function bigintsToNumbers<T>(value: T): T { return walk(value) as T }
function walk(v: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof v === 'bigint') return toCents(v)
  if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object' || v instanceof Date || ArrayBuffer.isView(v) || Prisma.Decimal.isDecimal(v)) return v
  if (Array.isArray(v)) { for (let i = 0; i < v.length; i++) { const w = walk(v[i]); if (w !== v[i]) v[i] = w } return v }
  const o = v as Record<string, unknown>
  for (const k in o) { const w = walk(o[k]); if (w !== o[k]) o[k] = w }
  return o
}
const BIGINT_MODELS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(Prisma.dmmf.datamodel.models.filter((m) => m.fields.some((f) => f.type === 'BigInt')).map((m) => m.name))
export const moneyAsNumbers = Prisma.defineExtension({ name: 'money-bigint-as-number', query: { $allModels: {
  async $allOperations({ model, args, query }) {
    const result = await query(args)
    const a = args as { include?: unknown; select?: unknown } | undefined
    return BIGINT_MODELS.has(model) || a?.include || a?.select ? bigintsToNumbers(result) : result
  } } } })
export function installBigIntJson(): void {   // safety net only; idempotent
  if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(BigInt.prototype, 'toJSON')) return
  Object.defineProperty(BigInt.prototype, 'toJSON', { value: function toJSON(this: bigint) { return toCents(this) }, writable: true, configurable: true, enumerable: false })
}
```
Checked behaviour:
- zMoneyCents throws AppError 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE through `.parse()`. Non-integers and sign violations stay ZodError, which surfaces as 400.
- toJSON gives {"x":2500000000}, and throws AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE for 2n**60n.
- The model-only heuristic is complete for Postgres model operations. A result carries a bigint only from its own model, from include/select (fluent calls arrive as `select`), or from aggregates of its own model.

The spec only says "expect exactly 22 statements" and never makes the builder fail when the output differs.
amendments.change: In §5, snapshot `prisma/schema.prisma` to the scratchpad IMMEDIATELY before the 40 money edits, and diff from that snapshot rather than HEAD. Then make it a hard check: the generated SQL must contain exactly 22 `ALTER TABLE … ALTER COLUMN … SET DATA TYPE BIGINT` statements over exactly the 40 listed columns, and nothing else (no CREATE, DROP, ADD COLUMN or index). Any other line aborts and goes to the orchestrator. Also confirm `git diff backend/prisma/schema.prisma` shows only Int→BigInt changes on the 40 fields plus comments.

amendments.problem: The moneyAsNumbers heuristic walks EVERY result that uses select or include, on all 196 models, and recurses into Json values. Many hot non-money reads use select/include with large Json: SiteLayout blocks/settings on every public storefront page, menus with modifiers, orders with items on KDS/expo polling. All of them get walked in full on every request, although only 23 models can hold a bigint. Customer, now a BIGINT model, is also walked including its Json fields. The 0–30% overhead was measured on 200k-row money reads, not on these hot paths.
amendments.change: Make the walk precise using the runtime DMMF the spec already relies on. Precompute, per model, (a) its BigInt scalar field names and (b) its relation fields with their target model. Then: convert only BigInt-typed scalar keys, recurse only into relation keys (arrays or objects, by target model) and into aggregate buckets (_sum/_min/_max of BIGINT models), and never descend into Json or other scalar fields. Also skip the walk when the model has no BIGINT field and no select/include path reaches a BIGINT model (compute reachability once at module load). Keep the current generic walk only as a fallback for unknown models. Add to the boundary test: a SiteLayout read with select returns the same object without walking its blocks (spy or timing not needed — assert a Json value containing a nested object identity is unchanged) and the existing number assertions still pass.

amendments.problem: §3a lists only the sites tsc reports. Several `_sum.<widened> ?? 0` / comparison sites typecheck but are bigint-sensitive, and the spec's own rationale is that toCents and sumCents keep code "correct on a raw client too". Examples: src/lib/chartOfAccounts.ts:205-207 (`debit !== credit` with `?? 0` on journalLine groupBy, which runs at BOOT for every company), and src/modules/financePlanning/routes.ts:131-142 (recalcLinePaid: `_sum.paidAmountCents ?? 0`, then `paid >= line.negotiatedCents` and a write back). These work under the boundary, but on a raw client they silently retire the wrong accounts, because `0n !== 0` is true.
amendments.change: Add to §3 a grep-based pass that tsc does not cover: every `_sum.`/`_max.`/`_min.` of the 42 fields across src goes through sumCents, wherever it appears (rg `_sum\.(amountCents|totalCents|paidAmountCents|...)`). Name at least chartOfAccounts.ts:205-206 and financePlanning/routes.ts:135. Assign them to agents A and C.

amendments.problem: §3b.2's single clamp in lib/exceptions.ts nulls any amount that is not a safe integer. Today, flags whose amount is computed with floating point (variance × cost, percentages) either save fine (Int columns reject non-integers, so the flag fails and is lost; flagException only logs a warning) or are lost. The new clamp keeps the flag but throws the money figure away for a plain fractional paisa value.
amendments.change: Clamp as `const a = input.amountCents; amountCents: a != null && Number.isFinite(a) && Math.abs(Math.round(a)) <= MAX_MONEY_CENTS ? Math.round(a) : null`. A finite fractional amount is rounded and kept; only non-finite or out-of-range values become null. Add a unit test: flagException with amountCents 1234.6 stores 1235.

built.summary:
BOOKS-06 is built: 40 money columns that were INT4 are now BIGINT. There is one boundary that hands every BIGINT back to the code as a plain JS number. The INT4 guard is lifted where it is no longer needed. tsc reports 0 errors and the full backend suite passes.

**Schema and migration**
- 40 Int→BigInt edits across 22 models. Defaults and nullability are unchanged. Each widened model has a one-line BOOKS-06 comment, and the BankStatementImport comment is updated.
- Before editing, I copied schema.prisma to the scratchpad and generated the migration by diffing against that copy. It contains exactly 22 `ALTER TABLE … SET DATA TYPE BIGINT` statements covering the 40 columns, and nothing else. `git diff` of the schema shows only Int→BigInt changes plus comments.
- New migration `backend/prisma/migrations/20261012140000_money_bigint/migration.sql`. Its header covers why, that values are kept with no backfill, the locking behaviour, a pre-deploy check, the P3009 recovery runbook (`migrate resolve --rolled-back`) and rollback. It sets `SET lock_timeout = '15s'` before the ALTERs (MIG-ROLLBACK-P3009).
- Rehearsed on a scratch DB, now dropped:
  - With a competing `LOCK TABLE journal_lines IN ACCESS SHARE MODE`, the migration failed after 15 s and everything rolled back (columns stayed integer).
  - A clean run kept ±2,147,483,647, NULLs and the default 0, left 42 bigint columns, and `migrate diff --exit-code` printed "No difference detected".

**The boundary: `backend/src/lib/money.ts` (new)**
- Ceilings: `INT4_MAX_CENTS` and `MAX_MONEY_CENTS` (PKR 900bn).
- Helpers: `toCents`/`sumCents` (they throw rather than round beyond 2^53), `amountTooLarge`, `assertMoneyFits`/`assertInt4Fits`, `zMoneyCents`/`zInt4Cents`, `bigintsToNumbers`.
- `moneyAsNumbers` uses the precise DMMF-driven walk from the WALK-SCOPE-PERF amendment. It descends only into relation keys whose target can reach a BIGINT model, and into `_sum`/`_min`/`_max`. It never visits Json.
- Deviation from the spec: a bigint at a row's own level is converted whatever its field name. That is safe because Prisma only produces bigint for BIGINT columns.
- Fix the spec's prototype did not hit: the fluent API (`findUnique(…).lines()`) reaches the extension as the source model with `select:{lines}`, but the result is already the unpacked relation. My first DMMF version left those values as bigint (found by the new test). It now follows single-relation select chains on single-record operations.
- `installBigIntJson` is the safety net. No `declare global` was added.
- `lib/prisma.ts` installs the boundary on the base client, under the RLS extension, so `prisma`, `serviceClient` and every tx carry it. Their types are unchanged.

**Code changes**
- All 122 tsc sites fixed with `toCents`/`sumCents` or helpers widened to `DbMoney`. No bigint literals, `BigInt()` or `as never` were added.
- Extra `_sum` sites that tsc does not flag (SUM-SITES-NOT-FLAGGED): `chartOfAccounts.ts` and `recipes/routes.ts:1408`.
- RAW-SELECT-STAR: `customer-channels.ts` and `supplier-channels.ts` now select ids in raw SQL and re-read the row through the model API.
- Guards:
  - **Lifted to MAX_MONEY_CENTS:** the journal engine (it also refuses entry totals that are not safe integers), the manual JE route, reconciliation split lines, statement balances and CSV lines (still `CSV_AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE`), PO totals, non-stock bill line costs and all bill totals, payments and applications, the supplier opening balance and the approval threshold.
  - **Added at MAX_MONEY_CENTS:** capex lines, projects, quotes, payments and capitalisation; opex; fixed assets; receivables, including amount + tax.
  - **Kept at INT4:** PO line unit cost, stock-linked bill line unit cost, receiving, and the till's `assertAmountsFit`. pos `MAX_AMOUNT_CENTS` now equals `INT4_MAX_CENTS`.
  - **New INT4 guard in `revalueItem`:** it returns 422 naming the item, with separate wording for a bill, a receipt and a void (the void message tells the user to adjust the item's cost first). The catch-up path's existing per-line catch reports it.
- FLAG-CLAMP-ROUND: the one flag-amount clamp in `lib/exceptions.ts` rounds fractional amounts and nulls only non-finite or out-of-range ones. The call-site clamps are removed.
- The old reconciliation `Number()`/`BigInt()` handling is removed, so there is one approach.
- Docs: the CLAUDE.md "Round 5" money bullet is replaced with the new rule. It carries the raw-SQL / `SELECT *` wording and a pointer to the P3009 runbook. `backend/src/lib/README.md` lists `money.ts` and updates the `prisma.ts` line.

All spec amendments are applied (1 must, 6 shoulds); none conflicted.
built.prodNotes:
**Deploy**
- Ship this with the new api image. entrypoint.sh runs the migration before the API boots.
- Rehearsed timing: about 1.5 s for 500k journal lines.
- Before deploying, check pg_stat_activity for other sessions on the box, and confirm free disk is greater than the size of journal_lines plus customers (the queries are in the migration header).

**If the migration fails**
- It gives up after 15 s on a lock.
- Prisma then records it as failed, and every image (old and new) refuses to boot with P3009.
- Fix before redeploying either image: `docker compose run --rm api npx prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20261012140000_money_bigint`.

**Rollback after a successful migration**
- Redeploying the previous images is safe; their INT4 guards just refuse new big amounts.
- Never write a down-migration.

**Clients and scripts**
- Clients still receive JSON numbers. No admin, tablet, storefront or mobile change is needed.
- Scripts that use their own `new PrismaClient()` would see bigint if they read widened columns; I checked and none do arithmetic on them. Any future script that reads these columns should use `serviceClient`.
built.ownerQuestions:
**The receiving case of the new INT4 guard cannot happen with real data.**
- On receiving, the item's new unit cost is an average of its current cost and the billed cost, both of which are already capped at INT4, so it cannot exceed INT4.
- The receiving test therefore edits the bill's recorded carried variance to force the 422. If you'd rather not keep a test that tampers with a record, it can be dropped.
- The bill and void cases do happen for real: an item whose cost was set by hand close to the limit, then a variance on top. Both give 422 and write nothing.
built.needsOtherFiles: None. I made one surgical edit to CLAUDE.md (only the Round 5 "Money inputs above INT4" bullet). The storefront workflow had not touched CLAUDE.md, and none of its files were modified. I ran `prisma generate` once against the shared client in node_modules; the orchestrator should know that client is now regenerated from the widened schema.

review.title: Big non-stock supplier bills (fit-out, equipment) are booked to 1210 Inventory – Food and counted as food purchases
review.scenario: createBill (around line 401) now lets a non-stock line (no inventoryItemId, no poLineId) go up to PKR 900bn. The comment and the new test both describe this as being for 'a fit-out lot, a piece of equipment'. But postSupplierBill (accounting/supplierPosting.ts, `inventoryCents = subtotalCents - usedCents`) books the whole subtotal of every bill as Dr ACCT.INVENTORY_FOOD (1210). Repro: tests/moneyBigint.test.ts section 3 posts a PKR 30m bill with one line, 'Kitchen fit-out', which gives 201 and Dr 1210 PKR 30,000,000.00. Effects: (1) the balance sheet shows PKR 30m of food stock that does not exist, and the capex never reaches the fixed-asset register or depreciation; (2) recipes/routes.ts:1400 reads 'actual purchases' as debits to 1210 (the `sumCents` line this diff touched), so the actual-vs-theoretical food-cost report for that period gains PKR 30m of food purchases. Booking bills to 1210 is an existing rule, but before this change the INT4 cap blocked these amounts in one line. This change raises the cap specifically for this case and has a test that asserts it posts. The test checks only that the entry balances, not which account it lands in.
review.fix: Choose one: (a) keep non-stock bill lines at the INT4 cap and send capex-scale purchases through CapEx payments and capitalisation, which already post to fixed assets and advances; or (b) add an account per non-stock line (an expense code or a fixed-asset category) and have postSupplierBill debit that account instead of 1210. In either case, change the 'Kitchen fit-out' test to assert the debit account as well as the balance.

review.title: TenantContribution.monthlyCents is still INT4 and has no AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE guard (raw 500)
review.scenario: This is a company-level money column that a group can exceed: the monthly head-office contribution from one company to another. The migration left it INT4, and its input at contributions.ts:74 is `z.number().int().nonnegative()` with no upper bound. A CEO who records a PKR 25m/month head-office contribution (monthlyCents 2,500,000,000) reaches tenantContribution.create/update and gets a raw Prisma 500 ('value out of range for type integer'), not a 422. The value also feeds projections/labour.ts and the opex payroll view. This breaks two parts of the brief: no money column a group can realistically exceed was widened here, and no INT4 column without its guard was flagged.
review.fix: Either widen tenant_contributions.monthlyCents to BIGINT in 20261012140000_money_bigint, read it with toCents, and use zMoneyCents on the input; or keep it INT4 and switch the input to zInt4Cents('The monthly contribution') so the request is a 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE rather than a 500.

fix.summary:
I confirmed both findings and fixed both. tsc is clean and the full backend suite passes: 129 of 129 files, 1982 tests passed, 4 skipped.

**MONEY-BIG-1 (confirmed, fixed with option a).** The finding is right. `postSupplierBill` books every bill's whole subtotal to 1210 Inventory – Food. My earlier change raised the cap on non-stock bill lines to PKR 900bn, so a PKR 30m "Kitchen fit-out" bill was posted as food stock. I did not take option (b) because it needs a new per-line account column, and this workflow only owns the money columns in the schema.

What `createBill` (backend/src/modules/procurement/service.ts) now does:
- **Non-stock lines** (no inventoryItemId or poLineId) are capped at INT4 (PKR 21,474,836.47) again. The cap applies to each unit cost, each line total, and the sum of all non-stock lines on the bill. Above it the request gets 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE, and the message adds that capital spend (fit-out, equipment) belongs in CapEx, not a supplier bill. The CapEx path is already built: payments post to 1340, and capitalising moves the item to the fixed-asset register.
- **Stock lines** keep an INT4 unit cost, but their line totals may be BIGINT. A group's bulk food purchase really is stock in 1210.
- The bill's subtotal, tax and total stay BIGINT.

The header comments in the service and the migration, and the BOOKS-06 note in CLAUDE.md, now say this.

Test changes:
- In tests/moneyBigint.test.ts (section 3), the fit-out test that asserted a 201 is gone. In its place:
  - A PKR 30m stock bill now checks which accounts it hits: Dr 1210 3,000,000,000, Dr 1320 GST input 540,000,000, Cr 2010 the amount due net of WHT, and the entry balances.
  - A PKR 30m fit-out line, a 200 × PKR 150k line and two PKR 15m non-stock lines are each 422, mention CapEx, and save no bill or journal entry.
  - A non-stock line at exactly the INT4 cap still records.
- In tests/booksRound5.test.ts, the bill test that expected non-stock amounts above INT4 to post is rewritten the same way, and now checks Dr 1210 too.

**MONEY-BIG-2 (confirmed, fixed by guarding rather than widening).** Without a cap, a PKR 25m/month contribution reached the insert and came back as a raw 500. In backend/src/modules/positions/contributions.ts, `monthlyCents` now uses `zInt4Cents('The monthly contribution')`. This covers POST and PATCH, which uses `.partial()`, so both now return 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE before any write. Negative or fractional amounts are still 400. I kept the column INT4: one company's monthly transfer to another is a per-company running cost, not a group balance, and widening it would also change projections/labour.ts, lib/labour-budget.ts and the opex `_sum`. The migration header and CLAUDE.md now list it as intentionally INT4 with its guard. New section (8) in tests/moneyBigint.test.ts tests this with an operator who belongs to both companies:
- create at PKR 25m is 422 and saves nothing;
- create at the INT4 cap is 201;
- PATCH to the cap plus 1 is 422 and leaves the stored value unchanged;
- a negative amount is 400.

I rejected neither finding.

**One more test fix, not from the findings.** The final full run failed `tests/auditLedgerFollowups.test.ts` (the sales-tax-return CSV test), and it failed the same way run on its own. It used a single UTC day as its date window. Just after midnight Karachi time, the test sale books to the previous business day while the manual entry books to today, so a one-day window misses one of them. I changed it to query yesterday through today in Karachi time; the assertions are unchanged. `salesTaxReturn.ts` only had the mechanical toCents/sumCents change in my diff.

Full backend suite against servd_test_bigint: 129 of 129 files passed, 1982 tests passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. tests/auditLedgerFollowups.test.ts failed consistently just after midnight Karachi time before its date window was widened, and passes after.
